The Malted Barley Slub Donegal is our new development for this season and is particularly special to us. When the current family member who runs the mill in Donegal found a sportcoat from the 40s using fabric his relative helped weave, he knew he wanted to bring it back to Ireland with him. At last years development meeting, he was showing us the fabric and we loved the depth of color, yarn irregularity, and overall finish of the fabric, so we wanted to redevelop something similar in a coating weight.
The fabric development started by working with these little puffs of raw wool, called "pads". With the pads, we're looking at both final yarn colors, as well as the colors of the flecks you find in Donegal Tweeds. Our "Devil's fit" slim straight cut jeans in 14oz indigo overdyed black selvedge denim. Utilising a double-twisted weft yarn (the same as our signature 21oz weave), this crisp, mid-weight denim provides exceptional durability and comfort straight off the rack without the lengthy break-in period commonly associated with our heavier-weight fabrics. This fabric is woven with rope-dyed indigo warp and white weft yarns — it may not be our heaviest denim, but it fades with the best of them!
To create this darkened variation, we take a pair of standard IH-666S-142 jeans and steep the entire garment in black dye using a sulphur dyeing process. This stains the indigo denim and stitching, and oxidises the metal hardware — with the added bonus of removing all shrinkage from the fabric. A unique middle ground between our traditional indigo and black denims, over time the fabric will gradually fade with blue-tinged hues in high-wear areas.
